notes: Account background: spun out of AgriData Inc. — builds real-time recommendations for grain merchants.
Primary objective: replace current CPU-based reranker with dedicated GPU pool to hit sub-150ms p95 for ranked results.
CTO quote (paraphrase): "We have seasonal peaks at harvest — throughput must scale predictably without 3x cost spikes."
They run sensitive customer contracts; need explicit data residency and audit logs for EU customers.
Prefer open-model variants (Llama-family & Mistral forks) with quantized fallbacks for cost control.

technical_requirements: Throughput target: sustained 200 qps for reranker pipeline (batching across 16 requests), peak bursts to 500 qps for 10 minutes
Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for single-turn rerank calls; p99 < 300ms soft target
Model options: 13B-70B family tested (fp16 + 4-bit quantized variants for fallback), prefer models with KV cache support
Reserved GPU planning: initial proposal 8x80GB A100 equiv (or 4xH100) with burst pool for seasonal demand
Autoscale policy: horizontal scale with reserved baseline + controlled burst; prefer capacity-based routing over pure CPU throttles
Availability: enterprise SLA with 99.9% uptime for dedicated pool; require maintenance windows & credits in contract
Logging/observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency histograms, trace for every request id
poc_plan: Phase 1 (week 0): environment provisioning — VPC peering, KMS proof-of-concept, service account setup
Phase 2 (week 1): synthetic load tests — validate throughput and batching configs on dedicated pool
Phase 3 (week 2): representative prompts + end-to-end rerank pipeline with customer dataset (anonymized)
Phase 4 (week 3): 48-hour soak test under 70% of expected peak to observe memory fragmentation and cache hit rates
Phase 5 (week 4): canary roll to production-facing routing for a subset of customers; monitor for regressions
Deliverables: benchmark report, recommended reserve size, quantization profile, SLO agreement draft
load_test_results_summary: Initial synthetic run (2026-02-20): sustained 220 qps using 12-request batching for reranker; p95=138ms; p99=305ms
Observed tail spikes during 500 qps bursts where p99 climbed to 780ms — attributed to JVM GC on client side and transient autoscale lag
KV-cache hit rate after warmup: 63% (improves to ~82% with targeted warm-up scripts)
Cost estimate from run: projected per-token cost down 28% vs current CPU baseline when using quantized fallback paths
soak_test_plan: Target: 48 hours at 70% baseline (140 qps sustained) with periodic 10-minute bursts to 450 qps
Metrics to monitor: GPU memory fragmentation, per-model latency distributions, retry/error rates, cache hit ratio
Failure criteria: sustained p95 > 200ms for >10 minutes; error rate >1% sustained; out-of-memory events
Actions on failure: escalate to infra, capture heap / kernel traces, switch traffic to lower-capacity quantized variant
representative_prompts: Reranker: input=10 candidate passages + query; prompt pattern heavy on domain tokens (chemical composition of fertilizers)
Chat-assistant: multi-turn guidances for contract negotiation with growers (avg prompt length 420 tokens)
Summarization: 3-5 page agronomy reports -> 150 token executive summary; needs factuality checks
Embeddings: dense vector of product specs + time-series sensor metadata for similarity lookup (batch embedding jobs night-window)
sla_items: Latency SLOs: p95 < 120ms (primary); define credits for violations beyond 99.9% availability
Throughput guarantees for reserved pool with documented burst behavior and warm-up times
Maintenance policy: 48-hour advance notice for non-emergency maintenance; emergency patch windows limited to 1 hour with fallback routes
Data residency & deletion commitments for EU customers; quarterly security attestation
Support: 24/7 incident manager contact during POC and 4-hour P1 response thereafter
additional_comments: Customer is pragmatic: willing to accept quantized fallbacks if Redwood can demonstrate <20% quality delta on reranker evals. Procurement timeline aggressive — wants contract signed by 2026-04 to align with budget cycle.
